def count_score_at_least_12(entries):
    """
    Imagine you run the espresso bar at a bustling neighborhood cafe, and at
    the close of every shift the register hands you a raw dump of the
    morning's orders. Take that dump in through the single parameter
    entries. Each element of entries is a list of exactly three values: a
    label (str), a score (int), and a factor (int). Read the label as the
    name the barista scrawled on the cup — Ana, Marco, whoever swung by for
    a flat white. Treat the score as the loyalty points the till stamped
    onto that order, a simple integer the point-of-sale machine computed
    from the size and price of the drink. Treat the factor as the
    promotional multiplier that was active when the order was rung up; the
    marketing team likes to fiddle with it during happy hour, and it
    travels along with every record whether anyone asked for it or not.

    Your manager has one question at the end of the day: how many orders
    earned a healthy chunk of points? The house rule is that anything
    hitting a dozen points counts as a serious order — the kind that gets a
    customer meaningfully closer to a free pastry. Determine the number of
    entries whose score is greater than or equal to 12 and return it as an
    int.

    Slow mornings happen, so the register may hand you an empty dump, and
    busy Saturdays may hand you a long parade of cups instead. Either way,
    tally the serious orders and report the count so the manager can update
    the chalkboard by the door before the afternoon rush rolls in.

    >>> count_score_at_least_12([])
    0
    >>> count_score_at_least_12([['Ana', 12, 5]])
    1
    """
